# Ādittajātaka (Ja 424)

**ID:** Ja 424  
**Section:** Jātaka (ja)  
**Collection:** Sutta  
**Title (Pali):** Ādittajātaka  
**tipitaka.org (CST):** [https://tipitaka.org/romn/cscd/s0513m.mul7.xml](https://tipitaka.org/romn/cscd/s0513m.mul7.xml)

## AI-generated Overview (from reference literature)

*This overview was drafted by an AI model from the cited scholarship and catalog data and may contain errors; verify against the sources before relying on it.*

The *Ādittajātaka* (Ja 424) is a canonical Jātaka tale belonging to the Aṭṭhakanipāta [Fausböll 1883; Fausböll 1897]. In later editorial and commentary references, it is also cited as the *Sovīrajātaka*—drawn from its narrative opening (*atīte Sovīraraṭṭhe*)—which was corrupted in certain manuscripts into the ghost title *Sucirajātaka* [Fausböll 1897]. The canonical verses open with the fire metaphor *ādittasmiṃ* ("when [a house] is burning down") [Fausböll 1883]. According to the nidāna, the Buddha recounted this tale while residing at Jetavana concerning the "incomparable gift" (*asadisadāna*) offered by the King of Kosala, who had carefully investigated and selected the supreme field of merit headed by the Buddha before bestowing his offering [Fausböll 1883]. Illustrating that the wise of old also gave gifts after examination (*viceyyadāna*), the Master recounted his past life as King Bharata in the Sovīra realm alongside Queen Samuddavijayā (identified as Rāhula's mother), who supported Paccekabuddhas and practiced lifelong liberality [Fausböll 1883].

Scholars have noted the narrative's emphasis on discriminatory giving, wherein the king provides for ascetics, brāhmaṇas, and the poor or wretched (*kapaṇa*), while conveying that gifts offered to spiritually accomplished mendicants produce superior merit compared to charity directed merely toward the ordinary poor [Fenn 1994].

 Rhys Davids 1917].

**Parallels and text reuse**

- Passage-level parallels: SN 1.33 Sādhusutta; SN 1.41 Ādittasutta; AN 3.52 Dutiyadvebrāhmaṇasutta
- Mentioned in: Pv 21 Aṅkurapetavatthu

**Sources**

- [Mrs. Rhys Davids 1917] Mrs. Rhys Davids, The Book of the Kindred Sayings, Vol. I (1917) — Notes the occurrence of the shared verses in the Āditta-Jātaka.
- [Fenn 1994] Mavis Lillian Fenn, Concept of Poverty in the Pali Canon (1994) — Analyzes the text's portrayal of gifts to religious mendicants versus the poor (kapaṇa).
- [Fausböll 1883] V. Fausböll, The Jātaka together with its Commentary, Vol. 3 (1883) — Provides the Pali text, incipit (ādittasmiṃ), nidāna, and character identifications (Bharatarājā, Samuddavijayā).
- [Fausböll 1897] V. Fausböll, The Jātaka together with its Commentary, Vol. 7 (Index) (1897) — Explains the alternate title Sovīrajātaka and the manuscript scribal error Sucirajātaka.
